note: KDWP state fishing lake (40-acre lake, 225-acre wildlife area) 5 mi S and 2.5 mi E of Ness City. Free primitive camping beside the gravel parking areas above the lake's west shore, with picnic shelters, a vault toilet, a boat ramp and a courtesy dock. Roads are dirt and rut when wet (1/2026 camper). FCFS, 7 nights at most. --Claude
summary: KDWP page (Wayback 2026-07-11): free primitive camping confirmed, 40-acre lake, vault toilet; KDWP camping page: free, FCFS, 7-night max (added). Note rewritten (the 'south and west shores' line isn't on KDWP's current page). Lakefront -> lakeview (downgrade). New phone and website.
flags: WATERFRONT lakefront -> lakeview (unsure, so down): imagery (2026-11-06) shows the only places a vehicle can stop are the gravel parking lots and the turnaround above the west shore. The main lot with the shelter at the pin is 40-50 m from the water across a scrubby, steep, rocky bank; the turnaround to the west is similar, and the lot by the vault toilet is about 50 m back. KDWP: 'Vehicles are allowed on maintained roads and in the parking areas only', so nobody can drive down to the shore. KDWP doesn't say where on the area camping is designated.
PHONE (none stored) -> 620-276-8886 (area manager Brent Clark, per the KDWP Goodman page).
PIN 38.3876,-99.8542 sits in the main gravel lot by the picnic shelter; fine. RV Life's pin (38.38464,-99.85624) is 350 m SW and further from the developed area.

WEAK SPOT: the page still carries a 4/26/2022 low-water fish-salvage alert, and its 'currently full' line dates from 10/9/2018. The imagery (undated) shows a full lake. The current water level is unknown.

DESIGNATED CAMPING: K.A.R. limits camping to 'designated camping areas', but the Goodman page only says 'camping (primitive)' and doesn't mark any area. The two KDWP brochures linked from the page (showpublisheddocument/364 and /366) 403'd live and have no Wayback capture, so they stayed unread.
SAND: none. Grassy, unlevel spots on dirt roads (1/2026 camper); fine for the sand rule, but a wet-weather access caveat is in the note.
